caption:
A free AI assistant that keeps your files on your own Mac just launched, and the whole app is open source.

It's called Local Code, and it comes from the developers of the image app Draw Things. They released it on October 28 after a public beta that began on September 12.

Here's how it works. You open the app and pick an AI model from the built-in selector. Once you use a local model, the app handles your prompts and files on your Mac instead of sending them to a cloud AI provider. The developers say there are no outside installs, sign-ins, API keys or extra servers to set up.

What can it do? Create presentations, generate images and videos, build charts and infographics, write or review code, update spreadsheets, and edit Word and PowerPoint files. It also includes a browser the assistant can use to navigate sites and complete tasks online.

If you allow it, it can read information from Mail, Messages and Notes, and make changes in Calendar and Photos. According to its documentation, Apple's App Sandbox restricts its access to other files and parts of the system.

The price is zero. You can get a direct download now at getlocalcode.app, and a Mac App Store release is coming soon. It's Mac only for now, and how good it is will depend on the model you choose.
